input_messages.content: Hello! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I would really like to fix this so I can send pictures to my family. Can you help me with that?
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I am currently abroad in France. Please let me know if you need any other information to assist me.

On the status bar, I see excellent signal strength with 5G, but the data is disabled. From the network status, airplane mode is off, the SIM card is active, and the cellular connection is connected with excellent signal on 5G. However, mobile data is not enabled, and data roaming is enabled. Wi-Fi is off and not connected. What should I do next?
Mobile data is now turned on, and the status bar shows "Data Enabled" along with excellent 5G signal. I will try sending an MMS message now.
I tried sending an MMS message, but it still cannot send. What else can we try to fix this?

Mobile data is enabled, and the connection speed is excellent at 275 Mbps. The APN name is set to "internet," but the MMSC URL, which is important for sending picture messages, is not set. Wi-Fi calling is off, and the messaging app has the necessary permissions for SMS and storage.

What should I do next to fix the MMS sending issue?
I have reset the APN settings and restarted my phone. What should I do next? Should I try sending an MMS now or check the APN settings again first?

After the reboot, the APN settings now show the MMSC URL is set correctly. I also tried sending an MMS message, and it went through successfully. The issue seems to be fixed now. Thank you for your help! Is there anything else I should know or do?

Thank you for letting me know about the roaming and data usage. I don't have any other issues right now. I appreciate your patience and help with fixing the MMS problem. Have a great day! 

###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
